finding.claim: update_doc calls can_edit() but discards the result instead of calling require_edit(), so no authorization check is enforced. Any user who reaches the route can overwrite any document's body.
finding.source: Any requester to PUT /doc/<doc_id> with a JSON body. The doc_id path parameter selects the target and request.json['body'] is the new content. They need no ownership or editor rights.
finding.sink: doc["body"] = request.json["body"] at docs.py:20, a write to the protected document.

trace.note: Route PUT /doc/<doc_id> is registered with no auth decorator.
DOCS[doc_id] is looked up with no ownership filter.
can_edit(g.user, doc) returns a bool that is ignored, so abort(403) is never called.
The document body is overwritten with attacker-supplied data.

finding.guards_checked: The sibling route update_title correctly uses require_edit (docs.py:27), which shows the intended control. No before_request hook, decorator or other middleware appears in this file. g.user is never set here, so it would come from an external hook that is not present. Even if one exists, it provides authentication only, not per-document authorization. A missing doc_id raises KeyError, which gives a 500 and is a minor issue only.
